page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.medium is a storage-optimized instance powered by a single-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor using the arm64 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, this dedicated CPU features 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 6.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:6 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

A defining characteristic of the is4gen.medium is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 937 GB NVMe SSD. This high-capacity local storage is paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance is optimized for both network and EBS performance, making it suitable for applications requiring high-density local storage without relying on external network-attached volumes.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between storage capacity and compute or memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance falls in the average range at 1499.99, but multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are positioned in the lower percentiles. Specifically, large-block memory read bandwidth is 19.51 GB/sec and write bandwidth is 9.76 GB/sec. Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 940.0 and 938.0, respectively, reflect weak to poor performance relative to larger instance classes. Redis SET operations achieve 1.21 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 1.13 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the is4gen.medium offers a high ratio of local NVMe SSD storage and memory relative to its single-vCPU compute allocation. This resource density makes it a practical choice for lightweight database workloads, local caching, and storage-intensive applications that do not require heavy parallel processing or high memory bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services is4gen.medium is a storage-optimized instance utilizing a single-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 6.0 GB of memory and a substantial 937 GB local NVMe SSD. While its single-core CPU performance is average, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the lower percentiles, with large-block memory read speeds at 19.51 GB/sec and write speeds at 9.76 GB/sec. The instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps and supports hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. Given its high storage-to-compute ratio and moderate memory allocation, the is4gen.medium is qualitatively cost-effective for storage-heavy, low-compute workloads. It is best suited for lightweight databases, distributed caching, and localized file processing where high capacity local NVMe storage is prioritized over raw processing power.
